analysis.investment_thesis: Solarium Green is a small-cap solar EPC play riding India's renewable tailwind with attractive ROE (23%) and reasonable P/E of 21.5x. However, without visible earnings growth data, the PEG is indeterminate — and civil construction/EPC is a thin-margin, lumpy-order business that rarely earns ten-bagger status without scale.
key_strengths: Strong ROE of 23% and ROCE of 20.1% — capital efficient for an EPC player
Sector tailwind: India's solar capacity build-out is a multi-year story consumers can see
High promoter holding (58.34%) signals skin in the game
key_risks: Solar EPC is a commoditized, order-book-dependent cyclical — not a true fast-grower franchise
Tiny ₹301 Cr market cap with negligible institutional ownership (FII 0.22%, DII 3.15%) = low visibility, high volatility
Incorporated only 2018 — no long execution track record through a full cycle
red_flags: Growth rate not disclosed — cannot compute PEG, the key decision metric
Industry classification as 'Civil Construction' suggests margins may compress as competition intensifies
analysis.detailed_analysis:
What's the story? India is building solar at a furious pace, and Solarium is a turnkey integrator catching that wave. At 21.5x P/E with 23% ROE, the valuation is reasonable IF earnings are growing 20%+ — which would give a PEG under 1.0, right in my sweet spot. The promoter owns 58% so alignment is there, and at ₹301 Cr market cap this is exactly the small-cap size where ten-baggers hide. That's the bull case.

The bear case is that solar EPC is not a Dunkin' Donuts-style repeatable franchise — it's a lumpy, bid-driven civil construction business where one lost tender can wreck a quarter. With only a 2018 incorporation, Solarium hasn't proven it can scale margins or working capital through a downturn. I'd want to see 3 years of 25%+ revenue/EPS growth, order book visibility, and stable margins before stepping in. Until then, this is a watchlist name, not a buy — do more homework on the order book before committing capital.
